# Quality control

## Read in the data

We will first read in the data processed in previous sections:

```{r read-data, message=FALSE}
images <- readRDS("/mnt/central_nas/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/myeloid_panel/data_analysis/images.rds")
masks <- readRDS("/mnt/central_nas/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/myeloid_panel/data_analysis/masks.rds")
sce <- readRDS("/mnt/central_nas/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/myeloid_panel/data_analysis/sce_MY_02.rds")
```

## Filter for tumor cells 

```{r}
# Type 
type_df <- colData(sce) %>% as.data.frame %>% select(PID, type) %>% unique() %>% group_by(type) %>% count() %>% arrange(desc(n))

ggplot(type_df, aes(x = reorder(type,-n), y = n, fill = type))+
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "black")+
  theme_classic()+
  #scale_fill_manual(values = metadata(sce)$colors$type)+
  ylab("Number of patients")+
  xlab("Type")
```

```{r}
# Subset sce to only contain primary tumor cells 
sce <- sce[,sce$type == "primary"]
```

## Image- and cell-level QC

### Image-level

**Area QC**
Another quality indicator is the image area covered by cells (or biological tissue).
This metric identifies ROIs where little cells are present. We can compute the percentage of image 
are covered by cells using the TMA masks measured with ilastik and cellprofiler. 

We can then identify ROIs that have unusually low cell coverage or number of cells.
These images can now be visualized using `cytomapper` or `cytoviewer`.

```{r cell-density}
#Load TMA tissue masks
tissue_area <- read_csv("/mnt/central_nas/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/myeloid_panel/tissue_masks/tissue_area_TissueSegmentation.csv") 

sce$tissue_area <- as.numeric(tissue_area$AreaShape_Area[match(colData(sce)$sample_id,str_split(tissue_area$FileName_Tissue_Mask, "_Pro",simplify = TRUE)[,1])])

cell_density <- colData(sce) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    group_by(sample_id) %>%
    summarize(cell_area = sum(area),
              tissue_area = mean(tissue_area)) %>%
  mutate(covered_area = (cell_area / tissue_area)*100) %>%
  mutate(n_cells = as.numeric(table(colData(sce)$sample_id))) %>%
  arrange(covered_area)

ggplot(cell_density) +
  geom_point(aes(reorder(sample_id,covered_area), covered_area, color = covered_area))+ 
  ylim(c(0, 100))+
  geom_hline(yintercept = median(cell_density$covered_area, na.rm = TRUE), linetype="dashed", color = "grey")+
  geom_hline(yintercept = quantile(cell_density$covered_area, na.rm = TRUE)[2],linetype="dashed", color = "grey")+
  geom_hline(yintercept = quantile(cell_density$covered_area, na.rm = TRUE)[4],linetype="dashed", color = "grey")+
  theme_classic(base_size = 15)+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())+
  ylab("% covered area")+ 
  xlab("")+
  scale_color_viridis()

ggplot(cell_density) +
  geom_point(aes(reorder(sample_id,n_cells), n_cells, color = n_cells))+
  geom_hline(yintercept = median(cell_density$n_cells, na.rm = TRUE), linetype="dashed", color = "grey")+
  geom_hline(yintercept = quantile(cell_density$n_cells, na.rm = TRUE)[2],linetype="dashed", color = "grey")+
  geom_hline(yintercept = quantile(cell_density$n_cells, na.rm = TRUE)[4],linetype="dashed", color = "grey")+
  theme_classic(base_size = 15)+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())+
  ylab("Number of cells per ROI")+ 
  xlab("")+
  scale_color_viridis()

## Visualize critical images
#Kick-out criteria:
#n_cells < 300, covered_area < 8, tissue_area < 150000?
#split acquisitions should also be excluded #str_detect(cell_density$sample_id, "split")
image_id_cri <- cell_density %>% filter(n_cells < 100 | covered_area < 8 | is.na(tissue_area)) %>% pull(sample_id)

# Normalize and clip images
cur_images <- images[names(images) %in% image_id_cri]
cur_images <- cytomapper::normalize(cur_images, separateImages = TRUE)
cur_images <- cytomapper::normalize(cur_images, inputRange = c(0, 0.2))

plotPixels(cur_images,
           mask = masks[names(masks) %in% image_id_cri],
           img_id = "sample_id",
           missing_colour = "white",
           colour_by = c("DNA1","panCK", "CA9","CD68","CD45RO_RA"),
           colour = list("DNA1" = c("black","cyan"),
                         "panCK" = c("black", "yellow"),
                         "CA9" = c("black", "magenta"),
                         "CD68" = c("black", "green"),
                         "CD45RO_RA" = c("black","blue")
                         ),
           image_title = list(cex = 0.8),
           legend = list(colour_by.title.cex = 0.7,
                         colour_by.labels.cex = 0.7), 
           save_plot = list(filename = paste0("/mnt/central_nas/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/myeloid_panel/data_analysis/03_QC/cell_density_QC_critical_images.png")))

# Retain images that look fine 
image_id_cri <- image_id_cri[!image_id_cri == c("ZTMA249.3_ZTMA249_ID_323_CX3Y11_328")]

#Remove outlying images and cells (n=1728 cells)
summary(colData(sce)$sample_id %in% image_id_cri)
sce <- sce[,!colData(sce)$sample_id %in% image_id_cri]
sce
```


```{r mean-expression-per-image, message=FALSE, fig.height=7}
# TMA 224.1 block C

sce$TMA_fine <- paste0(str_split(sce$sample_id, "_", simplify = TRUE)[,2],"_", str_split(sce$sample_id, "_", simplify = TRUE)[,3])

cur_sce <- sce[,sce$TMA_fine == c("TMA224.1_BlockC","TMA224.1_BlockB")]

library(scuttle)

image_mean <- aggregateAcrossCells(cur_sce, 
                                   ids = cur_sce$sample_id, 
                                   statistics="mean",
                                   use.assay.type = "exprs")

dittoHeatmap(image_mean, genes = rownames(sce)[rowData(sce)$use_channel],
             assay = "exprs", cluster_cols = TRUE, scale = "none",
             heatmap.colors = viridis(100), 
             annot.by = c("PID", "TMA_fine","subtype"),
             annotation_colors = list(PID = metadata(sce)$colors$PID,
                                      subtype = metadata(sce)$colors$subtype
                                      ),
             show_colnames = FALSE)

```


**Mean marker expression per image**

This check does not indicate image quality _per se_ but can highlight biological differences.

```{r mean-expression-per-image, message=FALSE, fig.height=7}
library(scuttle)

image_mean <- aggregateAcrossCells(sce, 
                                   ids = sce$sample_id, 
                                   statistics="mean",
                                   use.assay.type = "exprs")

dittoHeatmap(image_mean, genes = rownames(sce)[rowData(sce)$use_channel],
             assay = "exprs", cluster_cols = TRUE, scale = "none",
             heatmap.colors = viridis(100), 
             annot.by = c("PID", "TMA","subtype"),
             annotation_colors = list(PID = metadata(sce)$colors$PID,
                                      subtype = metadata(sce)$colors$subtype
                                      ),
             show_colnames = FALSE)

```



## Cell-level

**Cell size QC**
Next, we observe the distributions of cell size across the individual images. Differences in cell size distributions can indicate segmentation biases due to differences in cell density or can indicate biological differences due to cell type compositions (tumor cells tend to be larger than immune cells).
We also detect very small cells in the dataset and will remove them. The chosen threshold is arbitrary and needs to be adjusted per dataset.

```{r cellsize_dis, message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
colData(sce) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    group_by(sample_id) %>%
    ggplot() +
        geom_boxplot(aes(reorder(sample_id,area), area)) +
        theme_classic(base_size = 15) + 
        theme(axis.text.x = element_blank()) +
        ylab(~ "Cell area " (mu * m^2)) + xlab("")+
  geom_hline(yintercept = median(colData(sce)$area), linetype="dashed", color = "grey")+
  geom_hline(yintercept = quantile(colData(sce)$area)[2],linetype="dashed", color = "grey")+
  geom_hline(yintercept = quantile(colData(sce)$area)[4],linetype="dashed", color = "grey")

#Cell area range
summary(sce$area)

#Only keep cells with an area above 5 (n=2909 cells)
sum(sce$area <= 5)
sce <- sce[,sce$area > 5]
sce
```











## Clinical data quality control

### Add metadata

ZTMA20 has pN and pM information for a subset of patients. 

```{r}
library(readxl)
ZTMA20 <- read_excel("/mnt/central_nas/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/myeloid_panel/data_analysis/data/ZTMA20_BOD2022.xls")

ZTMA20$PID <- str_replace(ZTMA20$PathoNr, " ", "")

ZTMA20$pN_simple <- ifelse(ZTMA20$pN %in% c("0","1","2"), ZTMA20$pN, NA)
ZTMA20$pM_simple <- ZTMA20$pM

# Add this information to SCE 
sce$pN_simple <- ZTMA20$pN_simple[match(sce$PID, ZTMA20$PID)]
sce$pM_simple <- ZTMA20$pM_simple[match(sce$PID, ZTMA20$PID)]
```



### Subtype

```{r}

# Re-group subtypes 
sce$subtype_combined <- ifelse(sce$subtype %in% c("clear_cell_RCC", "papillary_RCC", "chromophobe_RCC"), sce$subtype, "other")
sce$subtype_combined[sce$subtype_combined == "clear_cell_RCC"] <- "ccRCC"
sce$subtype_combined[sce$subtype_combined == "papillary_RCC"] <- "pRCC"
sce$subtype_combined[sce$subtype_combined == "chromophobe_RCC"] <- "chrRCC"

metadata(sce)$colors$subtype_combined <- setNames(c("#63A8A0", "#A6CEE3","#C3AAD2","grey"),c("ccRCC","chrRCC","pRCC","other"))  

# Subtype 
subtype_df <- colData(sce) %>% as.data.frame %>% select(PID, subtype_combined) %>% unique() %>% group_by(subtype_combined) %>% count() %>% arrange(desc(n))

ggplot(subtype_df, aes(x = reorder(subtype_combined,-n), y = n, fill = subtype_combined))+
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "black")+
  theme_classic()+
  scale_fill_manual(values = metadata(sce)$colors$subtype_combined)+
  ylab("Number of patients")+
  xlab("Subtype")
```

### Survival of CC 

```{r}
sce$status_OS <- ifelse(sce$censor_dead_0_alive_1 == 1, 0, 
       ifelse(sce$censor_dead_0_alive_1 == 0, 1, sce$censor_dead_0_alive_1))

sce$OS_months <- sce$survival_months

sce$pT_combined <- sce$`pT12/34`
sce$`pT12/34` <- NULL 

sce$ISUP_combined <- ifelse(sce$ISUP %in% c("1","2"),"1/2", ifelse(sce$ISUP %in% c("3","4"), "3/4", sce$ISUP))
sce$lymphocytes_combined <- ifelse(sce$lymphocytes %in% c("1","2"),"1/2", sce$lymphocytes)
```

## Cell-level

**Cell size QC**
Next, we observe the distributions of cell size across the individual images. Differences in cell size distributions can indicate segmentation biases due to differences in cell density or can indicate biological differences due to cell type compositions (tumor cells tend to be larger than immune cells).
We also detect very small cells in the dataset and will remove them. The chosen threshold is arbitrary and needs to be adjusted per dataset.

```{r cellsize_dis, message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
colData(sce) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    group_by(sample_id) %>%
    ggplot() +
        geom_boxplot(aes(reorder(sample_id,area), area)) +
        theme_classic(base_size = 15) + 
        theme(axis.text.x = element_blank()) +
        ylab(~ "Cell area " (mu * m^2)) + xlab("")+
  geom_hline(yintercept = median(colData(sce)$area), linetype="dashed", color = "grey")+
  geom_hline(yintercept = quantile(colData(sce)$area)[2],linetype="dashed", color = "grey")+
  geom_hline(yintercept = quantile(colData(sce)$area)[4],linetype="dashed", color = "grey")

#Cell area range
summary(sce$area)

#Only keep cells with an area above 5 (n=2909 cells)
sum(sce$area <= 5)
sce <- sce[,sce$area > 5]
sce
```

**Staining artifacts**
Observing potential staining differences (e.g. between samples/batches) can be crucial to assess data quality. We will use ridgeline visualizations to check differences in staining patterns:

```{r stainingarti, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=20, fig.height=40}
#Randomly select 10 sample Ids for visualization
set.seed(22)
cur_id <- sample(unique(sce$sample_id), 10)

p1 <- multi_dittoPlot(sce[,sce$sample_id %in% cur_id], vars = rownames(sce)[rowData(sce)$use_channel],
               group.by = "PID", plots = c("ridgeplot"), 
               assay = "exprs", 
               color.panel = metadata(sce)$colors$PID)

plot(p1)
```

**Dimensionality reduction**
Finally, we will use non-linear dimensionality reduction methods to project cells from a high-dimensional (40) down to a low-dimensional (2) space. For this the scater package provides the runUMAP (and runTSNE) function. To ensure reproducibility, we will set a seed. For computing time, we will subsample to 10% of the cells.

**Goal:** Visualization of the low-dimensional embedding facilitates assessment of potential "batch effects". Should not be present in present cohort.

```{r dim_red, fig.width=15, fig.height=15}
library(cowplot)
## Subsample 10% of cells from each core 
# to save time and not get super crowded dimensionality reduction plots
set.seed(22)
sub_id <- colData(sce) %>% as.data.frame() %>% group_by("sample_id") %>% slice_sample(prop = 0.1) %>% arrange("sample_id") %>% pull(cell_id)
sce_sub <- sce[,sub_id]
sce_sub

#Run umap and tsne and save output directly into subsampled SCE
sce_sub <- runUMAP(sce_sub[rowData(sce_sub)$use_channel,], n_neighbors = 30, pca = 50,exprs_values = "exprs", external_neighbors=TRUE, BPPARAM = MulticoreParam())
sce_sub <- runTSNE(sce_sub[rowData(sce_sub)$use_channel,], exprs_values = "exprs", external_neighbors=TRUE, BPPARAM = MulticoreParam())

#Visualize
p1 <- plotReducedDim(sce_sub, dimred = "UMAP", colour_by = "PID")+
  guides(color="none")

p2 <- plotReducedDim(sce_sub, dimred = "UMAP", colour_by = "TMANr")+
  scale_color_manual(values = metadata(sce)$colors$TMANr)


p1+p2

plotReducedDim(sce_sub, dimred = "TSNE", colour_by = "sample_id")+
  guides(color="none")

#Visualize all marker expression
all_plots_UMAP <- lapply(c(rownames(sce_sub)[rowData(sce_sub)$use_channel]),
                    function(x){
                      p <- plotReducedDim(sce_sub, dimred = "UMAP", 
                                          colour_by = x, 
                                          by_exprs_values = "exprs",
                                          point_size = 0.5)
                      return(p)                    
                    })

plot_grid(plotlist = all_plots_UMAP)

all_plots_TSNE <- lapply(c(rownames(sce_sub)[rowData(sce_sub)$use_channel]),
                    function(x){
                      p <- plotReducedDim(sce_sub, dimred = "TSNE", 
                                          colour_by = x, 
                                          by_exprs_values = "exprs",
                                          point_size = 0.5)
                      return(p)                    
                    })

plot_grid(plotlist = all_plots_TSNE)
```

The modified `SingleCellExperiment` object is saved for further downstream analysis.

```{r save-objects-quality-control}
saveRDS(sce, "/mnt/central_nas/tnbc_volume/TNBC/data_analysis/03_sce_TNBC_QC.rds")
```
